record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.context_brief: Sets of sequences of a given complexity
record.original_question: Can one find an analogue of the FC algorithm in dimension d >= 4 that generates S-adic sequences of complexity (d-1)n+1 for almost every vector of letter frequencies?

evidence.quote: Can we ﬁnd an analogue of FC in dimension d >= 4, generating S -adic sequences with complexity (d- 1)n + 1 for almost every vector of letter frequencies?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For an infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$, the factor complexity $p_w(n)$ is the number of distinct factors of length $n$ that occur in $w$. An $S$-adic sequence is an infinite word produced by an infinite composition of substitutions $\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \ldots$ chosen from a finite or countable set $S$ of substitutions on $A$, in the sense that $w = \lim_{k\to\infty} \sigma_1\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_k(a_k)$ for suitable letters $a_k \in A$. For a word $w$ on a $d$-letter alphabet, the vector of letter frequencies is the vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d) \in \Delta_{d-1} = \{(x_1,\ldots,x_d) : x_i \ge 0,\ \sum x_i = 1\}$ where $f_i = \lim_{n\to\infty} |w_1\cdots w_n|_i / n$ (when the limits exist), with $|u|_i$ denoting the number of occurrences of letter $i$ in $u$.

A known three-letter construction (often called the FC algorithm), based on a multidimensional continued fraction algorithm, produces, for Lebesgue-almost every frequency vector $(f_1,f_2,f_3)\in\Delta_2$, an $S$-adic sequence on a 3-letter alphabet with factor complexity $p(n) = 2n+1$ for all $n\ge 0$.

Problem. For each integer $d \ge 4$, does there exist an algorithm analogous to the FC algorithm — specifically, a finite set $S$ of substitutions on a $d$-letter alphabet together with a rule (driven by a multidimensional continued fraction-type algorithm) for selecting an infinite sequence of substitutions from $S$ — such that for Lebesgue-almost every letter-frequency vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d) \in \Delta_{d-1}$, the resulting $S$-adic sequence has letter frequency vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$ and factor complexity $p(n) = (d-1)n + 1$ for all $n \ge 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The d=3 case (complexity 2n+1 for almost every frequency vector via a multidimensional continued fraction algorithm conjugate to Selmer / FC) is established. For d ≥ 4, no analogous construction producing S-adic sequences of complexity (d−1)n+1 for almost every frequency vector appears to be known; existing higher-dimensional algorithms (Arnoux–Rauzy–Poincaré, Brun, Selmer, etc.) do not achieve the minimal complexity (d−1)n+1 almost everywhere. Recent work (e.g. on symbolic codings of generic toral translations) addresses related but distinct questions, suggesting the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Set of Sequences of Complexity 2n+1
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of ternary sequences with factor complexity 2n+1 for any vector of rationally independent letter frequencies, constructed via an algorithm conjugate to the Selmer algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: The d=3 analogue (complexity 2n+1 for a.e. frequency vector) is established.

status_evidence.title: Factor complexity of S-adic words generated by the Arnoux–Rauzy–Poincaré algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Studies factor complexity of S-adic systems from the Arnoux-Rauzy-Poincaré algorithm in higher dimensions; complexity is not (d-1)n+1 in general.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional algorithms studied do not yield (d-1)n+1 complexity a.e.

status_evidence.title: Symbolic coding of linear complexity for generic translations on the torus
status_evidence.snippet: Almost every translation on the 2-dimensional torus admits a symbolic coding of linear complexity 2n+1; higher-dimensional analogues are conjectural.
